Small business website mistakes to avoid start with not focusing on what actually gets calls. You got a site, but nobody's reaching out to you. If you're tired of feeling invisible online, you need a simple plan that gets you found by the people actually looking for your service right now. We cut the fluff and show you how to get noticed.

Stop Wasting Time: The Top 3 Website Mistakes Killing Your Local Leads Your Google Business Profile is your storefront. Most local business owners set it up wrong. You might have photos that don't show your real work, or your hours are wrong. You aren't responding to reviews when people leave them. This is your most direct way to get found right now.

You're probably missing photos, messing up your hours, or ignoring reviews. This is the first thing you need to check. Get it right now so people can find you when they need your service. Your website doesn't tell people what to do. Tell them exactly what to do next. Make that action button impossible to miss on every page. Stop trying to rank for broad terms.

Instead of just "plumbing," try "plumber in Your City." Try "emergency leak repair near me." This tells Google exactly where you live and what you do. Set up a simple way to ask happy customers to leave feedback. Make it easy for people to leave a review. This helps you show up more often. If your site is slow on a phone, you're losing customers fast.

If your profile looks messy, people won't trust you. Get it right so you show up when someone searches for your service in your area. It should say Call Now or Book Appointment. If people have to hunt for what to do next, they leave. Stop trying to rank for broad terms.

Don't just target "plumbing." Target "plumber in Your City" or "emergency leak repair near me." Use what people actually type into Google. This is how you get found by local customers. Set up a simple way for happy customers to leave a Google review. A quick text message after a job is done works. Make it easy for people to tell their experience.

Finally, check your site on a phone. If your website takes more than three seconds to load on a phone, you're losing customers right away. Make sure your site works fast on any device.
